fields.meta_title: Recruitment Automation for Hiring Teams | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build recruitment automation that screens applicants, flags candidates stuck in review, finds past finalists, and holds offers above the pay band.
fields.h1: Build Recruitment Automation That Keeps Candidates Moving
fields.hero_description: Get recruitment automation that screens applicants and puts every hiring stage on a clock, built from a plain-English prompt.
fields.features_heading: The Hiring Steps Your App Takes Over
fields.features_subheading: Recruitment automation runs the repeatable steps of hiring, like screening and chasing slow reviews, while people choose who to hire.
fields.feature_1:
Knockout questions on each application

Ask yes or no questions about hard requirements, such as a driver's license. An applicant who answers no lands in a queue that a recruiter reads before any decline goes out.
fields.feature_2:
A clock on each hiring stage

Give every stage one owner and a time limit in business days. Once a candidate is overdue, the app alerts the stage owner in Slack or by email with everyone still waiting.
fields.feature_3:
Past finalists surfaced first

When a job opens again, the app searches your candidate records for people who reached the final round for it. Each one appears with the interviewer's notes from then.
fields.feature_4:
Offers held to the pay band

Store the minimum and maximum pay for each role and level. An offer above the maximum waits for the approver you name, who gets a direct Slack message showing the amount.
fields.feature_5:
Synced with your applicant tracker

The app syncs candidate records and offers with any applicant tracking system that has an API. Recruiters keep their usual screens while the rules run on the same records.
fields.feature_6:
Hiring rules you own as code

Candidate records live in a database your team owns. On paid plans, export the app's full code to your GitHub repository and review each hiring rule like any other code.

fields.tab_content_1:
103 of 142 applicants go on to a phone screen

Kestrelwood Home Care got 142 applications for a home health aide opening. Two knockout questions ask for a driver's license and weekend availability. The 39 who answered no to either wait in a decline queue that recruiter Ysolde Kwarteng reads before any email goes out. The other 103 go to her phone screen.
fields.tab_content_2:
8 days in review, and Tobiah gets a message

A candidate who sits in hiring manager review for more than 5 business days is flagged. Tobiah Okonkwo-Lund, who runs the north branch, gets one direct Slack message listing his 4 waiting candidates, the oldest at 8 days, with a link to each profile. Ysolde is copied on it.
fields.tab_content_3:
3 past finalists hear first when the role reopens

The scheduling coordinator job at Kestrelwood opens again this month. The app searched for candidates who reached the final interview for it in the last 12 months and found 3, each with the interviewer's notes attached. Ysolde writes to them before the job is posted publicly.
fields.tab_content_4:
No offer letter until Wenonah approves $81,500

The care team manager band tops out at $78,000, and the hiring team wants to offer $81,500. That puts the offer $3,500 over the maximum. The offer letter is not drafted until COO Wenonah Cadwallader approves the amount in a direct Slack message or sends it back to the team.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build recruitment automation that screens applicants and keeps each hiring stage moving, tested on past applicants first.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write knockout questions as yes or no
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every stage a candidate passes through: applied, phone screen, hiring manager review, interview, and offer. Next to each, note who acts on it today and how many days a candidate waits there. Start with the step where the wait is longest.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Phrase each knockout question as a yes or no about a hard requirement, such as weekend shifts for a care role. Keep it to 2 or 3 questions. Leave anything that needs judgment, like years of experience, to the recruiter's screen.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Import your current pay bands from the compensation spreadsheet, then name who approves an offer above a band. When compensation updates a band, the check reads the new numbers and no rule has to be rewritten.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the applicant tracking system your team already uses through its API. Candidates and stage changes sync into the app, and decisions made in the app sync back to the same records.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide who gets each alert and where it lands. One daily digest per hiring manager is easier to act on than a message for every candidate. Set Slack or email per stage, and change it by prompting.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run last month's applicants through the app before launch. Compare each knockout decision and reminder with what your recruiters did by hand. Where the two differ, adjust the rule by prompting and run the batch again.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go live with one busy role
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn the app on for your highest-volume opening first, and keep a recruiter reading every decline for 2 weeks. Once the queue holds no surprises, add the next role, then switch on the offer check.

faq_plan.q: What are the 7 steps of the recruitment process?
faq_plan.ref: What are the 7 steps of the recruitment process?

prov.original: What are the 7 steps of the recruitment process?

faq_plan.a: One common list has seven steps: identify the hiring need, create the job description, source candidates, screen and shortlist them, conduct interviews, make the offer, and onboard the new hire. Start recruitment automation with screening and the hand-offs between stages, since those repeat the same way for every candidate.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up recruitment automation?
faq_plan.a: Pick the hiring step that costs your team the most time, such as applications nobody reads for a week, and describe the rule that fixes it to Emergent's AI automation builder in plain English. Emergent builds the app and its database from that prompt. Add the next rule by prompting once the first one runs cleanly on real applicants.

faq_plan.q: What are the 5 steps of the recruitment process?
faq_plan.ref: What are the 5 steps of the recruitment process?

prov.original: What are the 5 steps of the recruitment process?

faq_plan.a: A five-step version folds interviews into screening: identify the hiring need, write a detailed job description, source candidates, screen applicants with resume reviews and interviews, then hold final interviews, check references, and extend the offer. Next to the seven-step list, it leaves out onboarding and treats the offer as part of the final decision.

faq_plan.q: How do I post new openings to social channels as part of a recruiting workflow?
faq_plan.a: Trigger the post from the job record. When a requisition is approved, the app drafts a post with the title and apply link, and a recruiter approves the wording before it goes out. The scheduling and approval steps are the same ones social media automation uses for marketing posts, with the job record as the source.

faq_plan.q: Which decisions in a hiring workflow should stay with a person?
faq_plan.a: Every decision about a specific candidate: who advances after an interview, who gets an offer, and any rejection that is not a plain fail on a hard requirement. Automate the routing and reminders around those calls. Log who made each decision and the date, for the day a candidate asks.

Recruitment automation is software that handles the repeatable parts of hiring on rules you set: sorting applications against fixed requirements, reminding the person who owns a stage, and checking each offer against its pay band. Your team still interviews the candidates and decides who gets hired.

faq_plan.q: How can recruitment automation handle job requisition approvals?
faq_plan.a: Route each new requisition through an approval workflow before the job is posted. The hiring manager submits the role and its budgeted pay, and HR or finance approves it or sends it back with a note. Only an approved requisition can be posted, and the approver's name and date stay on the record.

faq_plan.q: What should I automate first in recruitment?
faq_plan.a: Automate the stage where candidates wait longest, not the busiest one. Pull the last 3 months of stage dates from your applicant tracking system and compare the median wait at each step. A time limit and a reminder on that one stage save the most days. Emergent builds a first app for it from a prompt, and the free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: How do I measure whether recruitment automation is working?
faq_plan.a: Compare the days candidates spend in each stage, and the number who withdraw, for the month before launch and each month after. Also count how many knockout declines a recruiter overturns: a rising count means a question is too strict. Apps built with Emergent can show these numbers on a live dashboard.

faq_plan.q: Can recruitment automation create invoices after an agency placement?
faq_plan.a: Yes: trigger the invoice from the placement record. When a candidate's start date is confirmed, the app creates the invoice with the agreed fee and emails it to the client contact. Chasing unpaid invoices is the job of accounts receivable automation. Apps built with Emergent connect to your accounting software through its API.
